title: Route interaction canonicalization and schema evolution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Console emits multiple streams of user interactions (route open/close, preview, model call, throttled responses) across backend services and browser telemetry. Currently we have fragmented tables and denormalized views that make ML feature extraction and cross-tenant rollups brittle and expensive.

Goal: Introduce a compact, canonical route_interaction_fact and a small set of curated dimension/rollup tables that are optimized for: 1) deterministic lineage for audits and cost attribution, 2) efficient incremental backfills for schema evolution, and 3) straightforward feature extraction for usage-based ML and anomaly detection.

Scope: design the canonical event shape, deduplication rules (idempotency keys + semantic hashing), retention and partitioning strategy, schema evolution contract, and a CI-driven migration/backfill plan. Implement the first-pass ETL to populate canonical_route_interaction_fact and tenant_hourly_rollups, plus DDL and docs for downstream consumers (Console dashboards, billing pipelines, ML feature store).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical table canonical_route_interaction_fact created with stable primary key (event_hash) and minimal JSON payload column for extensible fields
Deduplication logic implemented in the ingestion layer: prefer event_id where present, otherwise use event_fingerprint computed from canonicalized path, tenant_id, timestamp bucket, and event_type
Partitioning strategy (by date + tenant shard) implemented and documented; retention policy enforced via scheduled compaction job
A curated tenant_hourly_rollups materialized table available with cost and latency aggregates used by billing dashboards
Migration plan and smoke backfill executed for last 90 days with progress dashboard and rollback knobs
API/Console consumers validated against the new schema with no visible regressions in top-5 dashboards
Data contracts and lineage metadata emitted to the data catalog (links available in the ticket)
implementation_plan: Design canonical event schema and map incoming streams -> canonical fields (1 sprint)
Build idempotent ingestion worker that deduplicates using event_id or event_fingerprint (2 weeks)
Create canonical_route_interaction_fact with partition/cluster keys and compaction policy (DDL + CI)
Populate tenant_hourly_rollups via an incremental aggregator job; expose revisioned materialized view
Run 90-day backfill on a narrow window to validate dedupe heuristics; keep safety window to compare with existing denorm tables
Add unit/integration tests in the ETL repo and a nightly e2e dashboard to monitor regressions
Coordinate with billing and ML feature owners for signoff and cutover plan
data_model_summary: Proposed tables: canonical_route_interaction_fact (event_hash:string, event_id:string, tenant_id:string, user_id:string, route:string, event_type:string, ts_utc:timestamp, truncated_payload_json:string, inferred_latency_ms:int, ingestion_source:string, processed_at:timestamp). tenant_hourly_rollups (tenant_id:string, hour_start_ts:timestamp, route:string, calls:int, succeeded:int, failed:int, avg_latency_ms:float, token_cost_units:float). route_session_map (session_id:string, tenant_id:string, first_ts:timestamp, last_ts:timestamp, events_count:int). The canonical fact stores small JSON in truncated_payload_json for rarely used fields to avoid frequent schema migrations.
partitioning_retention_policy: Daily partitions with tenant-shard clustering. Retention: full canonical fact kept for 90 days, compressed weekly snapshots retained for 365 days; rollups retained for 2 years. Compaction runs weekly to collapse duplicates in hot partitions.
schema_evolution_strategy: Use additive columns only; new fields appended to truncated_payload_json for 60 days then promoted to first-class columns after compatibility validation. All DDL changes routed through data-contract PRs and automated backwards-compatibility checks. Consumers must declare required_columns in the contract; unknown_columns allowed via payload column.
backfill_and_migration_notes: Backfill approach: run idempotent job that reads raw streams + existing denorm tables in parallel. Compare pre/backfill aggregates to validate dedupe. Use feature-flagged cutover: switch consumers to read-materialized-view pointing to canonical fact when parity thresholds met (>99.5% key aggregates). Backfill estimated compute: 1200 core-hours for 90 days; run in controlled pool over 48 hours with throttling.
observability_and_quality_gates: Emit ingestion metrics: events_in, unique_events_out, duplicate_rate, avg_processing_latency, backfill_progress. Add threshold alerts for duplicate_rate > 5% and parity drift > 1%. Create a data-quality dashboard in Console under 'Analytics -> Canonical Events'.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs: keeping a payload JSON avoids frequent DDL but shifts parsing cost to consumers. Aggressive compaction reduces storage but makes point-in-time recovery harder. We accept delayed point-in-time snapshots (weekly) to optimize cost. Deduplication heuristics may under/over-dedup edge cases — we will maintain an audit table of ambiguous events for manual review.
recent_updates: 2025-01-12: Schema draft reviewed with PM and ML feature owner; agreed to add inferred_latency_ms and ingestion_source fields.
2025-01-15: Implemented prototype dedupe algorithm in staging; initial duplicate_rate 2.3% on sampled week.
2025-01-18: Design review: decided to keep compact JSON payload for extensibility; raised TODO to schedule column promotion cadence.
2025-01-21: Integration test failures found around timezone normalization; fixed parsing in ingestion worker and re-ran sample backfill.
2025-01-24: PM signoff on migration plan pending final cost estimate; estimator PR linked above.
